name: Specific Purpose Visa -- Independent Means / Retiree Residency

requirements.blocker_text: Bolivia's Visa de Objeto Determinado (Specific Purpose Visa) covers non-tourism, non-work purposes including retirement, passive income, academic exchange, volunteering, religious activity, health, and family reasons, per Bolivia's own Foreign Ministry consular portal. For the independent-means/retiree purpose specifically, secondary sources converge on roughly USD 300/month in demonstrable financial means (bank statements or pension documentation) as the commonly-applied baseline, though this dataset found no officially codified minimum figure -- higher amounts reportedly strengthen the application. The visa itself is obtained at a consulate (valid 30 days for entry), then converted to Temporary Residency (1-2 years) at the Dirección General de Migración, requiring no absence exceeding 90 consecutive days.
requirements.fix_path: Document stable monthly income of at least USD 300 (pension, rental, or investment income), obtain the Specific Purpose Visa at a consulate, then convert to Temporary Residency on arrival.

outcome.duration_length: 1-2 years temporary, then convertible to permanent
outcome.physical_presence_requirement: no absence exceeding 90 consecutive days as a temporary resident; up to 2 consecutive years' absence permitted once permanent

sources.title: Bolivian Foreign Ministry consular portal -- confirms the Visa de Objeto Determinado's purpose list (including retirement/passive-income and family reasons), but not a specific income threshold

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Bolivia). STATUS: DRAFT -- the existence of this visa purpose is tier-1 confirmed, but the actual income figure is not: no officially published minimum was found anywhere in this build, consistent with the same 'no codified minimum' finding this dataset made for Paraguay's equivalent route. GENUINE FINDING: Bolivia's own Foreign Ministry groups retiree/passive-income, investor, academic, religious, and family purposes all under the SAME 'Objeto Determinado' visa category rather than issuing separate named routes for each -- this dataset modeled the retiree/independent-means purpose here specifically, and modeled the investor purpose as its own separate file (see bo_investor_residence.json) because Bolivia's own visa list additionally names a genuinely distinct 'Visa Múltiple' specifically for investment/business, giving that purpose its own real legal category unlike this one.
